scope: Bounded production local-inference cancellation, independent of minutes quality. Public fixture and read-only installed Qwen3-1.7B Q4_K_M/format1 Metal runtime; no user database or installed settings changed.

retained_failed_trials.failure: Engine and watchdog sent repeated SIGTERM; native log contains Received second interrupt and a Metal GGML_ASSERT. Original controller reported passed but native-exit-audit explicitly overrides that verdict.

errors: cancellation did not finish within the registered 5-second response budget
indeterminate: one token-producing incomplete request not observed
active cancellation/reaped release before shutdown not proven
retained_failed_trials.failure: The shared soft stop removed duplicate interruption, but the live SSE request stayed blocked through the unchanged five-second cancellation budget and five-second shutdown task grace. Native task cancellation was observed only around probe exit; closing the client socket is the inferred cause. Final process exit does not qualify this failed trial.

final_followup.native_process_identity_confirmed: exact executable + PID + creation time, independently included in sampled exit confirmation
final_followup.native_exit_status: not_captured; policy permits SIGKILL after grace, so no graceful-exit claim
final_followup.timing_scope: 1020 ms measures cancel to observing note_busy=false; before-shutdown worker release and subsequent task drain/process exit are separately verified, not assigned that exact duration.

validation.independent_review: no remaining P1/P2; stream EOF/process exit observation now shares the original five-second budget
controls: Real child observes exactly one soft cancellation across Engine and watchdog, both pooled and direct Server paths
Real loopback SSE continues after SIGTERM; production stream reader must unblock and the child must exit within the unchanged five-second budget
Repeated cancellation preserves the first deadline; no second force request
Cancellation between spawn and registration reaches the child before display PID publication
Closing/late-clearing old Server does not stop or unregister a new child
Exit observed by try_wait closes the force gate before Drop

limits: Process reaping is not a graceful-exit verdict. Native ExitStatus and internal Child.kill are not separately reported.
The five-second response gate is an observation budget, not an OS scheduling guarantee.
Summed RSS can double-count shared pages; sampled CPU misses unsampled tails. GPU allocations and energy were not measured. No speed, energy or quality improvement claim.
All raw failures remain preserved. No retry changes model, prompt, threads, context or acceptance deadline. Each subsequent native observation requires a changed cancellation implementation.
No installer, GPU component or model downloaded/built; CUDA/Vulkan remain separate optional components. No 0.3.5 release qualification.
change: Register each owned Server with a weak stop control. Engine cancellation and the watchdog share one synchronous soft-stop gate; registration rechecks cancellation after native spawn.

Keep the original stop cause and deadline. The existing watchdog prioritizes an accepted stop before resource/status sampling, allows one fixed second from the first signal, then requests at most one forceful stop if the owner has not closed the gate. Normal reader timeout is unchanged.

Serialize native signals with both production try_wait sites and Server Drop. Observed exit or wait errors close the gate before releasing it; clear the registration only when PID and control instance both match.

No additional watchdog thread, model call, retry, preference or database migration. The maintained inference_cancel_probe example observes real manual-generation content, cancellation and task drain; native process identity and exit remain independently checked by the runner.
